verdicts.reason: The class docstring's :param block lists only `topic` (which is not even a parameter) and `produce_to_pipe`; the newly added `max_processes` argument at line 47 is not documented there.

A repo-wide grep for `_create_process_for_shard\b` returns only its definition; `_ensure_processes_alive` (line 259) calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)` directly, so the singular method is an uncalled leftover.

Pre-PR the diff shows a single `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause})` per unhealthy detection; the new code loops `for shard in shards` and increments once per shard, so the counter is multiplied by the number of shards the process owns and gains a new `shard` dimension.
Same verified fact as c002: the method exists at lines 127-132, has no callers anywhere in the checkout, and only delegates to `_create_process_for_shards`.

In `join`, once `remaining_time <= 0` the loop `break`s, so every process after the current index never reaches the `terminate()` call at line 347 — exactly the scenario (a slow shutdown) where termination matters most.

`max_segments_per_shard = ceil(max_flush_segments / len(assigned_shards))` is computed per SpansBuffer; with N flusher processes each buffer now sees S/N shards, so each process's aggregate cap stays ~max_flush_segments and the system-wide cap becomes ~N x max_flush_segments instead of one global value.

The docstring asserts "Creates one process per shard", but the only production caller is the process-spans consumer whose `--flusher-processes` option has `default=1`, which flows to `max_processes=1` and yields a single process handling all shards.

The mechanical half is confirmed — each process builds its own `SpansBuffer` (own Redis client) and its own `KafkaProducer` — but whether the Kafka/Redis clusters have headroom and what N is planned needs the production capacity config and a rollout decision that are not in this repo.
Confirmed by grep across the checkout: `_create_process_for_shard` (singular) appears exactly once, at its definition on line 127.

The core assertion holds: `self.buffer` was removed and the constructor now reads only `buffer.assigned_shards` (three times) before building N fresh SpansBuffers, so `list[int]` would suffice. The trailing sub-claim is wrong though — `SpansBuffer.client` is a `cached_property` so construction opens no connection, and the passed-in buffer is separately used by `process_batch` in the parent (factory.py:80,90).

`max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` makes the in-code default one process per shard, while the CLI option defaults to 1; any caller constructing SpanFlusher directly (e.g. tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py:29) gets the per-shard behaviour implicitly.

Verified on CPython 3.11: `multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process(...)` is a `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` whose MRO is (SpawnProcess, BaseProcess, object), so `isinstance(p, multiprocessing.Process)` is False. The guard makes `process.kill()` unreachable, and a replacement is spawned for the same shards while the hung one keeps running.

The new test asserts only `len(flusher.processes)`, `max_processes`, `num_processes` and the shard-map total — all direct restatements of the constructor arithmetic — and never inspects `messages`, so multi-process flush correctness is untested. The parenthetical that `_ensure_processes_alive` is untouched is slightly overstated (test_basic's `step.submit` reaches it), but its restart/kill branch has no coverage.

The cited facts check out (both tests now use `django_db(transaction=True)`, run the flusher as real threads via `produce_to_pipe`, need Redis, and the monkeypatched `time.sleep` turns the flusher's `time.sleep(1)` into a busy loop — though that busy loop predates this PR). Whether they are actually flaky needs repeated CI runs against the real Postgres/Redis setup.
`cat -A` on the region shows an empty line immediately before the closing ``` fence; the diff's pre-image had the fence directly after `organizations.prefetch_related('projects')`.

The diff shows the pre-PR code calling `self.process.kill()` unconditionally; the new code wraps it in `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`, which is always False for spawn-context processes, so the kill is now a no-op in production — a genuine behavioural regression.

The test does `import time` and calls `time.sleep(0.1)` at line 62, after `monkeypatch.setattr("time.sleep", lambda _: None)` at line 15 replaced the attribute on the module object — so the added wait does nothing. (test_flusher.py avoids this by using `from time import sleep`.)
`_create_process_for_shards` and `_create_process_for_shard` differ by a single trailing 's' and sit 40 lines apart; the same fix (deleting the dead singular one) resolves this.

The click.Option uses bare `type=int` with no IntRange. I reproduced the constructor arithmetic: max_processes=-1 gives num_processes=-1, `range(-1)` yields an empty process_to_shards_map, and `i % -1 == 0` then raises KeyError: 0 at startup.
The hasattr/isinstance guidance is a general Python convention with no connection to the span flusher multiprocessing work that constitutes the rest of the diff.

`get_memory_info` calls `iter_cluster_memory_usage(self.client)`, which issues a cluster-wide INFO independent of assigned shards, so looping over N buffers repeats the identical query N times. The claim's own caveats are also right: used and available scale together so the ratio is unchanged, and the default `spans.buffer.max-memory-percentage` is 1.0 (options/defaults.py:2725-2729), so the block is normally skipped.

There is no pre-existing SpanFlusher default to fall back to — `max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` is introduced by this same diff, and pre-PR the flusher always ran exactly one process. `default=1` therefore preserves current production behaviour rather than 'forcing it back'; adopting the suggestion would silently multiply flusher processes on deploy.
Lines 185 and 195 tag the same `shard_tag` value as `"shard"` while line 199 tags it as `"shards"`, so the wait_produce timer is keyed differently from the other two.

`self.processes` is only ever assigned a started SpawnProcess or Thread at line 124, and I confirmed `bool()` is True for both (neither BaseProcess nor Thread defines __bool__/__len__), so `if not process: continue` can never fire.

A bare `time.sleep(0.1)` as the synchronisation point between the drift bump and `step.join()` is a timing-based wait; waiting on a condition (e.g. polling `messages`) is the correct fix, and it is the same fix that resolves the no-op problem in c017.

`shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` is the comma-joined shard set of the process, and it is attached to `spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes`, which fires once per produced segment. The set of distinct values depends on the partition assignment and the `--flusher-processes` value, so it changes on every rebalance.

Both branches reproduced against the constructor logic: 0 is falsy so `max_processes or len(...)` yields one process per shard, and -1 produces an empty process map followed by KeyError: 0. The option is declared with plain `type=int`, no IntRange.

Dead-code half confirmed by grep. The naming half is also right: the body looks up the owning process and restarts it wholesale via `_create_process_for_shards`, so it would disrupt every other shard mapped to that process, not just the one named.
